% The data, code and proofs statement, in paper 1's form (item 11, 2026-11-05).
% Every path is in the repository; every number here is a section's and is
% regenerated by the script that section names (paper3/README.md, "How to
% regenerate every number").
\section*{Data, code and proofs}
\label{sec:data}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Data, code and proofs}

Our scripts, logs, Lean files and the text of this paper are openly
available at \url{https://github.com/Alex-Linhares/MOSP_trough_SAT},
under \repofile{paper3/}, with the companion Lean under
\repofile{lean/MOSPFormalization/SubexpPathwidth/}; the code and the
proofs are open source under the MIT licence. Everything this paper
reports can be re-run from there, and most of it can be checked without
re-running. The repository holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item a script for every number in the paper, under
  \repofile{paper3/scripts/}, one per section
  (Sections~\ref{sec:statement}--\ref{sec:related}); each reads the
  manuscript's extract and the clone with plain file reads, executes
  nothing of theirs, and has a \texttt{-{}-check} mode that verifies every
  page, line and quoted fragment the section cites and exits non-zero
  if any has moved; \repofile{paper3/README.md} lists the command beside
  each number;
\item the replay of Section~\ref{sec:replay}: the two sandbox scripts
  and the two second-checker scripts verbatim, the launch commands and
  the timeline (\repofile{paper3/replay/README.md}), the short logs,
  the axiom output, the version lines and the hashes
  (\repofile{paper3/replay/logs/}); the full build log and the exported
  environment are too large to commit and are identified by their
  SHA-256 hashes, which are committed, and a script
  (\repofile{paper3/replay/counts.sh}) that recomputes every count of
  that section from the log;
\item the companion Lean of Section~\ref{sec:lean}: the two files, the
  axiom audit that prints the axioms of every declaration the paper
  names (\repofile{paper3/lean/axiom_check.lean}) with its committed
  output, and the byte-level re-diff of the copied model against the
  clone (\repofile{paper3/lean/rediff.log}); Appendix~\ref{app:lean}
  lists the names;
\item the measurement of Section~\ref{sec:practitioner}: every call's
  seconds and result (\repofile{paper3/latex/tables/practitioner_raw.csv}),
  the versions, machine and load of the run of record
  (\repofile{paper3/latex/tables/practitioner_meta.json}), and the
  script that regenerates the formulas from their seeds and re-runs it;
\item the two audits the paper rests on, with their scripts and the
  committed text extract of the manuscript
  (\repofile{reports/scratch/eth_audit/}), and the four public texts
  Section~\ref{sec:related} quotes, as fetched, with their hashes
  (\repofile{paper3/related/fetched/});
\item the record of every question the writing could not settle, one
  numbered entry each, in \repofile{paper3/ETH_AMBIGUOUS.MD}; and the
  report of the blind reading of the whole paper against its sources,
  in \repofile{paper3/refuter/}.
\end{itemize}
The object of the paper is not ours. The OpenAI collection is read-only
at commit \texttt{4eaee875} of \url{https://github.com/openai/math}
(Apache-2.0 licence); the challenge file, the solution tree, the scope
note and the manuscript are cited from it by file and line, and nothing
in it was modified. A reader who wants to repeat the replay needs the
collection at that commit, the pinned Lean release and the Mathlib
revision Section~\ref{sec:replay} names, a sandbox such as the one the
scripts use, and about an hour of eight cores.

\paragraph{What this does not claim.} The statement above says what is
available and how it is checked. It does not say that every reader will see the
same seconds. The timings of Section~\ref{sec:practitioner} and the
replay's 33 minutes are one machine's. Only the counts, the hashes
and the axiom lines are expected to repeat exactly.
